_comment: Evidence-backed classification overrides for kinola.py, applied BEFORE the default
classifier so an entry decides rather than argues with it. Two directions:
`include` publishes a film whose page fills no metadata field, `exclude` withholds an
event the classifier would otherwise publish. The second is why the mechanism cannot
Scope is a provider id plus the site's own /film/{slug}/ identifier. Never a title
keyword: classifying on a word is what the adopted policy forbids, and a keyword list
here would reintroduce it through the back door.
Every entry carries action, reason, evidence and verified. `evidence` names where the
claim was read and `verified` the day it was read, so a stale entry is visible rather
than merely old. An override that no longer changes the default decision is redundant
and tests/test_kinola.py fails on one; an event leaving the programme, or a page that
cannot be read, is not by itself proof of that.
The decision and the corrections behind it: docs/archive/2026-09-providers.md,

overrides.reason: A documentary screening whose page fills no metadata field, so the classifier leaves it unresolved.
overrides.evidence: kinolaika.fi/film/a-fox-under-a-pink-moon/ names it in prose: "Esitettavana elokuvana on Mehrdad Oskouen dokumenttielokuva A Fox Under A Pink Moon (2025)", with 76 min, K-16 and English subtitles beside it. Director, form and year are all stated; only the labelled fields are missing.
